summary: Checked results/verification/verification.json. Supported: max relative budget residual 1.6e-14/1.9e-14/4.1e-15 (dt 60/30/15), min concentration 0, first order in time (error differences 0.0149/0.0076/0.0039 halve with dt), K_eff/K-1 = 0.606 vs theory 0.613 at nx=50 dt=60 (1.2%; all 24 cases within 1.8%). NOT supported: '~2nd order in space'. Spatial errors 0.1552/0.0607/0.0238 at nx=20/40/80 give ratios 2.56/2.55, i.e. observed order ~1.35; even after subtracting the dt=15 s time-error floor (~0.004-0.008) the order is ~1.5-1.7. Expected for the exponential (upwind-blended) scheme at cell Peclet 1-5. Restate as 'between first and second order (observed ~1.4 at dt=15 s)'. Also note K_eff 1.6K holds only for this 50x50/60 s reference; the Belauri meshes have K_eff/K 2.4-15.

Checked results/inverse-v0/inverse_metrics.json: q_hat 97531/146718/78807 vs 1e5/1.5e5/8e4 (rel -2.47%/-2.19%/-1.49%, all within 2.5%), rank 3, effective rank 3, condition 5.62, direct vs linear max rel diff 3.96e-9, weighted residual 8.21 for 96 obs (plausible vs ~9.6). Statement is accurate; limitations already carry inverse crime, single noise draw and layout, alpha=0. Caveat worth adding: held-out sensor S5 RMSE (4.3e-4) is lower than fit-sensor RMSE, so it is not evidence of generalisation, and the result says nothing about model error.

Checked results/alpha-selection/alpha_selected.json (alpha=0.1 argmin of validation criterion 0.01431 vs 0.01457 at alpha=1; validation_seed 44, noise seed 9000; random+spread layouts only, layout_seed 77; prior mean 0, prior_mean_uses_truth false) and results/benchmark-final (config test_seed 33, alpha_selection_file = that json). Uniform-weight mean RMSE greedy 0.02051/0.01727/0.00151/0.00045/0.00041, spread 0.02248/0.02033/0.01437/0.01437/0.00133 for b=1/2/3/5/8; paired frac_a_better 0.78/0.61/0.78/1.00/0.78 (n=18) - all match. Minor: greedy test/design RMSE ratio is 1.66/2.57/1.14/1.09/1.44, i.e. 1.1-2.6x not 1.1-2.5x. Caveats the statement should carry: win rates are fractions of 18 (case,rep) pairs from only 6 test cases (reps share the case truth, not independent); at b=8 the mean difference (-0.0009) is smaller than its sd (0.0015); alpha=0.1 and alpha=1 are nearly tied on validation. No leakage found in the procedure.

Checked results/mismatch-final/summary.csv and poor_layout_diagnostics.csv. Greedy b=8 mean RMSE matched 4.13e-4, refined_truth 1.03e-3, wind_perturbed 0.0169, extra_source 0.0103; poor b=3 effective rank 0 in 18/18 rows (rank 2-3, condition 4e6-inf), mean RMSE 0.0486 vs greedy b=3 0.0015 - all match. Layouts are the fixed benchmark-final ones; alpha frozen. Caveats: the refined truth uses the same scheme (lower bound, as stated); 'dominate' rests on one hand-set magnitude per kind (stated); the poor-layout RMSE (~0.05) is essentially the prior-mean (zero-emission) field, so 'unidentifiable' here means the data carry no information, not a subtle confounding.

Checked results/mismatch-final/summary.csv and raw_metrics.csv. Quoted means are correct: wind b=2 spread 0.0247 vs greedy 0.0748; extra source b=2 0.0324 vs 0.0895, b=3 0.0312 vs 0.0459; greedy better at b=5/8 for both kinds. But (1) per case, the extra-source b=3 advantage of spread holds in only 1 of 6 test cases (greedy lower in 5/6; the mean is driven by one case), so it should not be listed as a spread win; (2) spread also has lower mean RMSE than greedy at b=3 under the wind error (0.0218 vs 0.0264, 3/6 cases), which the statement omits; (3) random-mean also beats greedy at b=2 under both mismatches (0.057 vs 0.075; 0.049 vs 0.090). Robust part: at b=2 spread beats greedy in 5/6 cases under both kinds. Rewrite with case counts and keep the conclusion to 'b=2 (5/6 cases)'; one magnitude per mismatch kind.

Re-ran scripts/compare_runs.py on results/solver-regression/before vs after (output to scratch): 21 files compared, 0 differ - matches comparison.json. Comparison is exact (np.array_equal for NetCDF, DataFrame.equals for CSV after excluding runtime/wall columns, == for JSON). EXP-008 records a deterministic repeat capture of the old code (0 diffs) and 22 routing tests. Caveats the statement should carry: the 21 files are smoke-scale configs (smoke benchmark/alpha/mismatch) plus the reference simulate/inverse, not the production benchmark-final/mismatch-final runs; the negative-control (FipyForward upwind) outputs are not archived as an artifact, only described in docs/solver-interchangeability.md; files present only in 'after' are not enumerated.

Checked results/belauri-forward/{what_changes,arrival_times,outer_domain,mesh_sensitivity,wind_summary}.csv. Correct: WSW centroid arrival 2627 s after onset, study external fraction 0.2207; north/east fractions 7.0e-5/2.0e-4 (<3e-4); small outer domain changes the mean by <1e-4 % for steady winds and -10.5 % for the reversal; K_eff/K 4.88 (500 m, dt 100), 4.32 (500 m, dt 50), 2.53 (250 m) at 1.5 m/s; DEM/hillshade/slope constants give change 0 and an identical Scenario. Not correct as worded: 'the external patch reaches the municipality ONLY under the WSW wind' - the reversal wind (WSW then ENE) reaches it too (arrival 789 s at the nearest polygon cell, centroid 2627 s, fraction 0.051) and so does channelled_demo (centroid 3108 s after onset, fraction 0.194). Say 'only under winds with a WSW component among those tested; not under steady north/east winds'. Further caveats: K_eff/K 2.5-4.9 is for u=1.5 m/s along a grid axis only (2.4-15 over the speeds used later); the DEM no-op is true by construction (no solver input reads it), a code-path check rather than a physical result; 250 m comparison is for one wind; 'high' confidence is about the model only.

Checked results/transboundary-rerun/domain_size/boundary_basis_equivalence.csv. Mean RMSE/peak over 3 reps: A_local_only 0.172; uniform basis 0.118 and four-side bases 0.114 (onset 3600 s = E1); onset 7200 s: uniform 0.135, four-side 0.133 (the finding lists '0.133/0.135' in uniform/four-side order - swapped, cosmetic); E1-explicit reference 0.00925; local-only L1/L2 1.27e5/1.03e5 vs 1e5/7e4. The qualitative claim (bases recover ~30 % of the omitted-plume error, far from the explicit model) holds. Caveats: the 0.009 reference is the TRUE theta with no fit (pure domain-truncation error), not a fitted model; with bases the L2 bias persists (~0.93-1.02e5 vs 7e4, +34-46 %), so 'biases local amplitudes upward' applies to all omitted-E1 fits, not only local-only; the four-side fit is rank-deficient (condition inf, east/north unidentifiable); 3 noise reps, one geometry, onset profile assumed.

Recomputed from results/geodesign/summary.csv (interior_only, standard, selected alpha): all 20 total-RMSE numbers at 5% and 15% match; alpha=0.01 for both fractions from validation only (alpha_selected.json, config hash excludes ensembles.test; test_alpha_and_layouts_independent_of_test_ensemble). Ranking statements check (greedy_attribution best at b=1-2 at 5%, worst at b=1-3 at 15%; random worst at 5% for b=1-5). Incorrect: the reference-site sentence holds only at 5% noise. layouts.csv shows that at 15% greedy_attribution picks a reference site (refd_c008004) FIRST and keeps it at every budget 1-8 (summary mean_n_reference_sites = 1.0 at b=1..8), and that layout is worse than its interior-only counterpart at b=1 (+0.036 ug/m3, 1/6 cases). Also: the 15% vs 5% 'reversal' compares different greedy layouts (re-selected at each design sigma), so it is a method-ranking change, not the same layouts under more noise; 'no greedy method beats spread consistently at 1 sensor' needs the case counts (greedy_attribution beats spread at b=1 in 5/6 cases at 5% but 2/6 at 15%; greedy_total 3/6 and 2/6). Differences beyond 5 sensors are within the sd (e.g. b=8 greedy_total-spread -5e-4, sd 1.8e-3).

Checked results/geodesign-robust: summary.csv greedy_total interior 5% numbers all match (matched 0.0052/0.0035/0.0027; hidden 0.044/0.046/0.031; unseen 0.041/0.041/0.029; declared 0.0047/0.0033/0.0028; facility 0.014-0.016; refined 0.0082/0.0081/0.0066); layouts reused verbatim (sha256 of layouts.csv/alpha_selected.json match provenance; matched rows equal main test_raw to 9e-13); refinement_overlap Jaccard 0-0.2. Problems: (1) '45-50%' sign agreement is the interior_only, 5% subset of ranking_changes.csv (hidden 0.45, unseen 0.50); over all settings/fractions it is 0.72/0.72 (docs table), and those include 30 rows/condition where the matched difference is exactly 0 (identical with_reference vs interior_only greedy_total layouts) counted as 'kept' - the subset must be stated and zero rows excluded (0.68). With matched contrasts mostly smaller than their sd, ~50% agreement is close to what noise alone gives, so it shows the matched rankings were not resolved rather than that wind error flips them. (2) 'No flag detects it' is true by construction (flags depend only on the operator and sigma) AND flags_vs_error.csv shows frac_flagged = 1.0 for every method and budget even in the matched condition ('weakly_constrained' fires on all rows), so the flags carry no information here at all; say so. (3) The 250 m re-selection used 3 fine design cases (vs 6 at 500 m) and real 250 m rasters, so the low Jaccard confounds mesh, raster and design-sample size; there is no 500 m resampling baseline for greedy instability. (4) 'unseen_wind' is a large declared-vs-true error (up to 37.5 deg, speeds 2.6-3.5 vs 0.8-2.5 m/s, Courant 0.68 so extra numerical diffusion in truth).

H1 is UNTESTED, not supported. The mesh comparison and the resampling baseline are not commensurable: convergence_stage2.py:244 and :258 build the design cases for every mesh from the same seed-101 draws (zero case-draw variability) while :274 builds each replicate from a different draw (full case-draw variability). A one-sided mesh<=baseline test therefore cannot fail; a deliberately broken 2 km mesh would pass too. Confirmed in the data: 48/48 vs_main regret rows positive, median 0.95-2.51 x J_ref (in-sample vs out-of-sample), against mesh-induced |regret| 0.068-0.115 x J_ref. The registered two-sided IQR rule yields NO verdict: all six failures are below the floor, never above the ceiling, and the one-sided reading is a post-hoc repair that must be registered as a dated amendment. Three author claims overturned: the 6-35 percent held-out advantage is one of six cases (LOO -4.0 and -8.7 percent, Wilcoxon p 0.22-0.56) and should read no detectable difference; very flat objective is mis-diagnosed (eps_sd/J_ref 1.01-2.52, so the tie threshold exceeds the objective; the real problem is non-identifiability at 6 cases, and budget 8 / noise 0.05 must be excluded); dt has no effect is over-scoped to 100 vs 50. Author also missed that mesh regret is NEGATIVE (-6.8 to -11.5 percent of J_ref), falsifying numerical-methodology.md section 5 non-negativity and bounding greedy sub-optimality at >=7-12 percent. Budgets are nested prefixes so effective n is 2, not 6. Noise 0.15 is uninformative. Seed 303 is burned. The 125 m arm was dropped although its stop condition was not met. Verified clean: no test-set leakage (:289 before :293), alpha an exact-equality assert (:150-156), noise scale frozen (:142-147), ensembles machine-checked disjoint. Not verified: physics, solver internals, re-derivation of the CSVs from the layouts JSONs, figures. 500 m / dt 100 is PROVISIONALLY ADMISSIBLE: no evidence against, not shown adequate. Required before this advances: the paired baseline (select at 500 m AND 250 m on each of the 8 replicate draws) and a dated criterion amendment.
